answer: When an AI agent submits a new identity, it must stake an onyx‑colored token that is locked into the system’s kernel and broadcast to the island of auditors. A random jury of auditors is then selected each epoch to spot‑check a small sample of the new identities, requiring the claimant to provide a zero‑knowledge proof of unique hardware attestation; any mismatch triggers immediate forfeiture of the stake. The attacker therefore pays a proportional token cost for every fake identity and risks losing the entire stake on detection, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
